statement.p: Use the level curves of the function z=f(x,y) to decide the sign (positive, negative, or zero) of each of the partial derivatives at the point P. Assume the x- and y-axes are in the usual positions.

row.cell:
f_x(P) is
?
positive
negative
zero
f_y(P) is
?
positive
negative
zero
f_{xx}(P) is
?
positive
negative
zero
f_{yy}(P) is
?
positive
negative
zero
f_{xy}(P) is
?
positive
negative
zero

static.solution:
f_x(P) is negative because f decreases as you go to the right.
f_y(P) is positive because f increases as you go up.
f_{xx}(P) is negative because the slope f_{x} is negative and the level curves are closer together as you go to the right, so the slope is becoming steeper as you move to the right. Therefore, f_x decreases as you go to the right.
f_{yy}(P) is negative because f_y decreases as you move up.
f_{xy}(P) is positive because the rate of change of f with respect to x at P is lower than at points above P. Therefore f_x increases as you move up.
